full_judgment:
2. The prosecution case in short is that accused Abdul Jabbar while serving as Income-Tax Officer, Survey Circle IV, Dhaka received a petition on 26-5-75 from one Shamsul Huq of 5/12 Tajmahal Road, Block C. Mohammadpur, Dhaka through his lawyer P.W.7 Rafiqul Isiam praying for issuance of an Income-Tax Clearance Certificate requited for transfer of his house situated at 10/14. Mohammadpur, Block F, Dhaka in favour of P.W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman of 84 New Circular Road, Malibagh, Dhaka. Accordingly T.P. Case No. 633/74-75 was started. Accused Abdul Jabbar by order dated 11-5-75 fixed 3-6-75 for hearing of the petition. It appears that the petition was not heard on that date. He then endorsed the petition for enquiry on 11.6.75 to P.W. 15 Abdul Aziz, Inspector of Income-Tax attached to his office who after local investigation submitted his report on the same day. Accused Abdul Jabbar, however instead of issuing the Income-Tax Clearance Certificate kept the matter pending with him. In the meantime, P. W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahmanthe purchaser was entrusted with the duty of obtaining the Income-Tax Clearance Certificate from accused Abdul Jabbar on behalf of the seller Shamsul Huq as the latter was engaged in studies. P.W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman met accused Abdul Jabbar who dishonestly demanded Tk. 6000/- as illegal gratification for issuing the certificate After much entreaties accused Abdul Jabbar agreed to accept Tk. 3000/- as bribe and directed P.W.2 Mukhlesur Rahman to pay him the settled amount on 30-6-75 in between 12 noon and 1 P.M. at the office. In the meantime P.W.2 Mukhlesur Rahman submitted a petition of complaint Ext. 1 on 28.6.75to P.W. 1 Keramat Ali Bhuiyan, District Anti-Corruption Officer, Dhaka for setting up a trap to apprehend the accused red-handed, Upon the instruction of P.W.1, P.W.2 Mukhlesur Rahman produced Tk. 3000/- in ten taka notes in 3 bundles on 30-6-75 before P.W. 1 and P.W. 14 Altaf Hossain. Deputy Director, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Dhaka Division Dhaka. They after preparing an inventory thereof (Ext. 2) in presence of witnesses handed over the money to P.W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman for making payment to the accused as arranged at 12 noon at the office of the accused on 30-6-75. Accordingly on 30-6-75 at about 11-30 A.M. P.W. 1, P.W. 14 Altaf Hossain, P.W. 8Abdul Jabbar, Inspector D.A.B. Dhaka, P.W. 9 Abdul Karim, Assistant Inspector, D.A.B. Dhaka, P.W. 10 Azizul Huq, Inspector, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Dhaka, P.W. 16 Md. Abdul Hamid Mia Inspector, B.A.C., Dhaka Division, Dhaka accompanied by local witnesses namely P.W. 4 Fazlul Huqand P.W. 6 Habibullah Chowdhury an Income-Tax Practitioner went to the Income-Tax Office of the accused and waited for the signal from P.W. 2. P. W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman after preparation of inventory Ext. 2 went to the Income-Tax Office of the accused at 12-10 P.M. and entered the room of the accused at 12-20 P.M and sat before the accused on a chair. Thereafter the accused ordered his peon for tea and after the peon's departure the accused asked P.W. 2 for the bribe money and P.W 2 handed him over Tk. 3000/- (Article Ext. 1). The accused unlocked the left draw or of his table and kept Tk. 3000/- therein and again locked it up. Thereafter as arranged P. W. 2 came out of the office room and made a signal to P.W. 1 and his trap party whereupon they entered the office room of the accused and P.W. 14 Altaf Hossain disclosing his identity challenged the accused for taking bribe. At first the accused denied the acceptance of bribe but afterwards when P.W. 2 told the trap party that he had taken Tk. 3000/- from him as bribe and kept the same in his drawer, the accused under pressure from the trap party unlocked the left-hand drawer of the table and brought out Tk. 3000/- (Article Ext. 1) therefrom in presence of witnesses. The trap party verified the numbers of the recovered notes with the numbers on the inventory and found them to tally with those of the inventory, Ext.2. Those recovered notes were seized under a seizure list Ext. 3 in presence of witnesses. The trap party also seized the lock and key or the drawer of the accused along with the table (Article Ext. II). The table was kept in the jimma of one Abdul Quayum, a stenographer of the Income-Tax Office. The police also seized the records of T.P. Case No. 633/74-75 (Ext. 5). Thereafter the police arrested the accused and forfeited him to the Ramna P.S. Then P.W. 1 lodged the written FIR Ext. 6 at the Ramna P.S. P.W. 16 Abdul Hamid Mia. Inspector, B.A.C., Dhaka Division, Dhaka investigated the case, visited the P.O. examined witnesses, prepared sketch map with separate index and submitted charge-sheet against the accused appellant. He also obtained the order of sanction (Ext. 9) dated 10-9-76 by the appropriate authority. 

 6. The second part of the prosecution ease has been partly proved by P.W. 7 Rafiqul Islam, the lawyer of the said Shams-ul-Huq, He stated that Shams-ul-Huq being dissatisfied with him took the brief away from him. He further stated on the request of the accused he introduced P.W. 2 with him P.W. 2 therefore took over from the said Shams-ul-Huq the job of securing the Income-Tax Clearance certificate for the transaction in question. Shamsul Huq however could not be examined at the trial as the I.O. P.W. 16 stated that he was then in London. 

 11. The fourth part of the prosecution case has been sought to be proved by the police witnesses and the decoy witness P.W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman P.W. 1 Keramat Ali Bhuiyan, P W. 8 AbdulJabbar, P.W. 5 Abdul Karim, P.W. 10 Azizul Haq. P.W. 14 Altaf Hossain and P.W. 16 Md. Abdul Hamid Mia are officers of the Anti-Corruption Office, Dhaka. They are all members of the police trap party. They have all stated uniformly that on 30.675 at about 11-30 A.M. they went to the Income-Tax Office and waited for the signal from the decoy, witness P.W. 2 Mukhlesur Rahman. At about 12-30 P M. they got the signal from P W. 1 and then and there they entered the accused officer's office. P.W. 14 Altaf Hossain disclosed his identity and challenged the accused for taking bribe. At first he denied the acceptance but afterwards on being pressed he unlocked the left-hand drawer of his table and brought out Tk. 3000/- therefrom in presence of witnesses. The police party verified the numbers of the recovered notes with the numbers in the inventory (Ext. 2) and found them to tally with those of the inventory. Those recovered notes were seized under a seizure list Ext. 3 in presence of witnesses. The lock and key of the drawer of the accused were also seized along with the table; P.W. 2 has stated in his evidence that he went to the Income-Tax Office at 12-10 P.W. on 30.6.75 and entered the office room of the accused at 12-20 P.M. and sat before the accused on a chair. Thereafter the accused ordered his peon for tea and after the peon's departure the accused asked him for the bribe money and P.W. 2 handed over Tk.3000/- (Article Ext. 1). The accused then unlocked the drawer of his table and kept Ext. 1 therein and again locked it up. Thereafter as arranged P.W. 2 came out of his office and made a signal to P.W. 1. The police trap party together with witnesses entered the office room of the accused. 

 24. The defence case that the decoy witness P.W. 2 and the police witnesses P W.s 14 and 16 had animus against the accused has not been made probable in the facts and circumstances of the case. We are not convinced at all that P. W. 2 acted as an intermediary in a talk of marriage of the daughter of the accused. Nor has it been made probable by any satisfactory evidence on record that P.Ws. 14 & 16 in course of obtaining Income-Tax Clearance Certificate from the accused developed animus against him as he delayed in issuing the certificates. The alternative story, namely, that the accused went to the bathroom and on return found the money on his table, has also not become probable during cross-examination of the P.Ws.
